Project Title

Nationwide Epidemiological Pattern Clustering and Outbreak Prediction with Pandas, Seaborn, and Gradient Boosting Trees
Project Ref: ai-ml-ds-KTvmxLqoZep
File Name: nationwide_epidemiological_pattern_clustering_and_outbreak_prediction.py

Problem Domain

This project sits at the intersection of epidemiology, public health informatics, and AI. It involves:

  • Clustering historical disease incidence patterns across various regions.
  • Forecasting future outbreaks.
  • Informing public health preparedness.

Frameworks Used

  • pandas: for data ingestion, transformation, and preprocessing
  • seaborn & matplotlib: for multivariate exploratory data analysis (EDA)
  • scikit-learn: for clustering and preprocessing
  • XGBoost or LightGBM: for highly accurate gradient boosting trees
  • geopandas: for spatial analysis
  • joblib: for model persistence and inference pipelines

Use Cases

  • Cluster regions by disease progression similarity.
  • Forecast future outbreaks or spikes.
  • Visualize the spread trajectory on a national map.
  • Trigger alerts for healthcare resource allocation.

Example Input and Output

Input:

| region_id | date       | disease    | cases | deaths |
|-----------|------------|------------|-------|--------|
| 001       | 2024-01-01 | influenza  | 58    | 2      |
| 001       | 2024-01-02 | influenza  | 77    | 1      |
| 002       | 2024-01-01 | measles    | 6     | 0      |
...

Output:

  • Clustered regions with similar patterns.
  • Model predicting outbreak probability for next 14 days.
{'region_id': '001', 'outbreak_risk_next_14_days': 0.91, 'cluster': 2}

Key Learnings / Research Areas

  • Geospatial Clustering
  • Gradient Boosting Forecasting
  • Time Series Aggregation
  • Multivariate Health Informatics
  • Real-world feature engineering
  • #EpidemiologyAI #PublicHealthDataScience #GradientBoosting #SpatiotemporalClustering #PandemicModelling #DataDrivenHealthcare

Full Development Lifecycle

  1. Data Acquisition: API-based disease incidence data or open health data repositories.
  2. ETL & Preprocessing: Normalize and fill missing time series values by region.
  3. EDA: Identify seasonal and regional variances.
  4. Clustering: KMeans/DBSCAN on PCA-transformed features.
  5. Feature Engineering: Lags, rolling windows, exponential smoothing.
  6. Model Training: Train XGBoost/LightGBM models per disease.
  7. Evaluation: LogLoss/AUC/Confusion matrix per region.
  8. Visualization: Regional maps, time series spikes.
  9. Deployment: Batch scoring jobs with alerts.

Sister Projects

  • Disease Spread Simulation with SEIR + Agent-Based Models
  • Hospital Load Forecasting using Time Series ML
  • Pandemic Sentiment vs Case Curve NLP Project

Integration Ideas

  • Tableau/Power BI dashboards
  • SMS/email alerting system via Twilio or Slack
  • National Health Portals for policy triggers

Current Date: 2025-05-23

Timeframe: 4–6 weeks (for initial deployment), extendable for live ingestion systems

Final Product

  • A predictive dashboard and API system that allows public health analysts to:
  • View regional clusters.
  • Access next-week outbreak risk scores.
  • Trigger visual alarms for imminent surges.

Bonus Functionality

✅ Expert-Level Implementation:

  • Include SHAP values for explainability of outbreak predictions.
  • Temporal ensemble models combining multiple boosting strategies.
  • Multi-indexed pandas dataframes for efficiently managing disease-region-date hierarchies.

Where to Go from Here

  • Integrate mobile symptom checker data.
  • Enable live retraining from national health surveillance feeds.
  • Add transformer-based anomaly detection.
  • Extend to global epidemiological alerts system.

# ai-ml-ds-KTvmxLqoZep
# File: nationwide_epidemiological_pattern_clustering_and_outbreak_prediction.py

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import geopandas as gpd
import xgboost as xgb
import joblib
import warnings
import datetime as dt
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, accuracy_score, confusion_matrix
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from typing import Tuple, List, Dict, Any

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# --- Constants and Configuration ---
REGION_DATA_PATH: str = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datasets/geo-countries/master/data/countries.geojson"
EPIDEMIC_DATA_PATH: str = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/owid/covid-19-data/master/public/data/owid-covid-data.csv"
PREDICTION_WINDOW_DAYS: int = 14

# --- Load Data ---
def load_epidemic_data() -> pd.DataFrame:
    df: pd.DataFrame = pd.read_csv(EPIDEMIC_DATA_PATH, usecols=["location", "date", "new_cases", "new_deaths"])
    df = df.rename(columns={"location": "region", "new_cases": "cases", "new_deaths": "deaths"})
    df = df.dropna(subset=["cases", "deaths"])
    df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"])
    return df

def load_geo_data() -> gpd.GeoDataFrame:
    return gpd.read_file(REGION_DATA_PATH)

# --- Preprocessing ---
def preprocess(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df["cases"] = df["cases"].clip(lower=0)
    df["deaths"] = df["deaths"].clip(lower=0)
    df = df.groupby(["region", "date"]).sum().reset_index()
    df["cases_7d_avg"] = df.groupby("region")["cases"].transform(lambda x: x.rolling(7, min_periods=1).mean())
    df["deaths_7d_avg"] = df.groupby("region")["deaths"].transform(lambda x: x.rolling(7, min_periods=1).mean())
    return df

# --- Feature Engineering ---
def generate_features(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    features = []
    for region, group in df.groupby("region"):
        group = group.sort_values("date")
        for i in range(PREDICTION_WINDOW_DAYS, len(group)):
            window = group.iloc[i - PREDICTION_WINDOW_DAYS:i]
            target = group.iloc[i]
            feature: Dict[str, Any] = {
                "region": region,
                "date": target["date"],
                "future_cases": target["cases"] > window["cases"].mean() * 1.5,
                "mean_cases": window["cases"].mean(),
                "std_cases": window["cases"].std(),
                "mean_deaths": window["deaths"].mean(),
                "std_deaths": window["deaths"].std(),
                "case_trend": (window["cases"].iloc[-1] - window["cases"].iloc[0]) / (PREDICTION_WINDOW_DAYS + 1),
                "death_trend": (window["deaths"].iloc[-1] - window["deaths"].iloc[0]) / (PREDICTION_WINDOW_DAYS + 1)
            }
            features.append(feature)
    return pd.DataFrame(features)

# --- Clustering ---
def perform_clustering(df: pd.DataFrame, n_clusters: int = 5) -> pd.DataFrame:
    cluster_features: List[str] = ["mean_cases", "std_cases", "mean_deaths", "std_deaths", "case_trend", "death_trend"]
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(df[cluster_features])
    pca = PCA(n_components=2)
    X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X_scaled)
    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=n_clusters, random_state=42)
    df["cluster"] = kmeans.fit_predict(X_pca)
    return df

# --- Model Training ---
def train_model(df: pd.DataFrame) -> Tuple[xgb.XGBClassifier, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    features = ["mean_cases", "std_cases", "mean_deaths", "std_deaths", "case_trend", "death_trend"]
    X = df[features]
    y = df["future_cases"].astype(int)
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=42)
    model = xgb.XGBClassifier(use_label_encoder=False, eval_metric="logloss")
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    return model, X_test, y_test

# --- Evaluation ---
def evaluate_model(model: xgb.XGBClassifier, X_test: pd.DataFrame, y_test: pd.Series) -> None:
    y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
    auc = roc_auc_score(y_test, y_pred)
    acc = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)
    cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred)
    print(f"AUC: {auc:.4f}, Accuracy: {acc:.4f}")
    print("Confusion Matrix:\n", cm)

# --- Visualize Clusters ---
def plot_clusters(df: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    sns.set(style="whitegrid")
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
    sns.scatterplot(data=df, x="case_trend", y="death_trend", hue="cluster", palette="deep")
    plt.title("Regional Clustering Based on Epidemiological Trends")
    plt.xlabel("Case Trend")
    plt.ylabel("Death Trend")
    plt.legend()
    plt.show()

# --- Main Pipeline ---
def main() -> None:
    raw_data: pd.DataFrame = load_epidemic_data()
    print("Loaded epidemic data")
    preprocessed_data: pd.DataFrame = preprocess(raw_data)
    print("Preprocessed data")
    feature_data: pd.DataFrame = generate_features(preprocessed_data)
    print("Generated features")
    clustered_data: pd.DataFrame = perform_clustering(feature_data)
    print("Performed clustering")
    model, X_test, y_test = train_model(clustered_data)
    print("Model trained")
    evaluate_model(model, X_test, y_test)
    joblib.dump(model, "epidemic_predictor.joblib")
    print("Model saved")
    plot_clusters(clustered_data)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Above, the project code for "Nationwide Epidemiological Pattern Clustering and Outbreak Prediction with Pandas, Seaborn, and Gradient Boosting Trees" has been created. Let me know if you'd like a breakdown, visualization enhancements, or to generate a report or dashboard from this.
